title: RBI steps in to keep rupee from slipping to record low, traders say - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
The rupee was at 96.7575 ​per dollar ‌in early trading, little changed on the day, but averted a fall ‌to its record low of ​96.96 hit in May. | Photo Credit: FRANCIS MASCARENHAS

The Reserve Bank of ​India likely intervened in the ‌FX market on Friday ​to support ⁠the rupee as the currency neared its all-time low, three ‌traders told Reuters, with the unit battered ‌by persistent portfolio outflows ‌and ⁠elevated oil prices ⁠due to the Iran war.

The rupee was at 96.7575 ​per dollar ‌in early trading, little changed on the day, but averted a fall ‌to its record low of ​96.96 hit in May.

State-run banks were ⁠spotted offering dollars right before the local spot ‌market opened, most likely on behalf of the RBI, the traders said.

The central bank had been a regular ‌presence in the foreign exchange ​market over the last several sessions. However, persistently ⁠elevated oil prices, portfolio ⁠outflows and higher US Treasury yields have ‌continued to pressure the rupee.
